newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS - Reed-Elsevier buys law titles from Thomson.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Reed-Elsevier buys law titles from Thomson.

text.p: Anglo-Dutch publishing group Reed-Elsevier said on Wednesday it had agreed to buy some 40 U.S. law publications from Canada's Thomson Corp.
Reed-Elsevier said U.S. anti-trust authorities had ordered Thomson to sell off the titles in return for aproval of Thomson's 1996 acquisition of West Publishing Co.
The publications, which include U.S. Supreme Court Reports, generated sales revenues of $49 million in 1996. Reed-Elsevier described them as "established and profitable".
"The acquisition provides another opportunity for the company to broaden its spectrum of legal information and provide industry-leading sources, in any medium," it said.
Elsevier deputy chairman Paul Vlek said the acquisition would immediately enhance Reed-Elsevier's earnings.
"We can say that this is profit-enhancing from the start," he told Reuters.

Vlek said Reed-Elsevier and Thomson had agreed not to disclose the financial terms of the acquisition, but he added that Reed-Elsevier had obtained a good price because of Thomson's position as a forced seller.
Vlek said Reed-Elsevier, through its Lexis-Nexis unit, and Thomson/West were the two biggest online law publishers in the U.S. with about 50 percent of the market each.
He said Thomson/West was by far the biggest U.S. law publisher in terms of print media but that Reed-Elsevier was a small but growing hard-copy law publisher in the U.S.
